plain_english: Surely, when their gross form is suddenly burned away, things forcibly attain unity with the great blazing light of awareness by their very nature; this is regarded as the supreme offering in the Bhairava tradition.
sanskrit_cite:
nūnaṃ jhaṭiti saṃpluṣṭasthūlarūpatayā haṭhāt /
yānti bodhamahājvālāprakāśaikyaṃ svarūpataḥ /
sa eṣa paramo homo bhairavīyakrame mataḥ // [AgMsv_2.132]

plain_english: When entities are properly offered by method into the fire within one's own awareness, they abandon the division of difference and, by their own power, kindle that very fire.
sanskrit_cite:
nijabodhajaṭharahutabhuji bhāvāḥ samyagsamarpitā yuktyā /
jahati bhedavibhāgaṃ nijaśaktyā taṃ samindhate yasmāt // [AgMsv_2.133]

plain_english: Whatever sense-object consciousness creates before itself by its own will and by the force of its creative nature becomes fit for meditation on that very object.
sanskrit_cite:
yad eva svecchayā sṛṣṭisvābhāvyavaśataḥ puraḥ /
nirmimīte 'kṣaviṣayaṃ taddhyānāyāvakalpate // [AgMsv_2.134]

plain_english: For although the abode of consciousness is formless and yet made of all forms, for those who seek results some particular form is established as the object of meditation.
sanskrit_cite:
nirākāre hi ciddhāmni viśvākṛtimaye sati /
phalārthināṃ kācid eva dhyeyatvenākṛtiḥ sthitā // [AgMsv_2.135]

plain_english: Just as, even within a nondual and full reality, someone fetching water eagerly seeks a pot by setting aside other forms, so too a particular form may be chosen.
sanskrit_cite:
yathā hy abhedasaṃpūrṇe bhāve 'py udakam āharan /
anyākṛtyapahānena ghaṭam arthayate rasāt // [AgMsv_2.136]

plain_english: In the same way, through the unfolding of the supreme Lord's self-restriction, some particular form gives rise to some particular conception of a result.
sanskrit_cite:
tathaiva parameśānaniyatipravijṛmbhaṇāt /
kācid evākṛtiḥ kāṃcit sūte phalavikalpanam // [AgMsv_2.137]

plain_english: But for one whose activity is the fullness of consciousness and who desires no result at all, meditation in the form of the whole universe unfolds at all times.
sanskrit_cite:
yas tu saṃpūrṇacidvṛttir na phalaṃ nāma vāñchati /
tasya viśvākṛti dhyānaṃ sarvadaiva vijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_2.138]

plain_english: For the Kula yogin reeling from the intoxicant of the surging Bhairava essence, whatever arises, in whatever way it arises, simply arises.
sanskrit_cite:
kulayogina udriktabhairavīyarasāsavāt /
ghūrṇamānasya yaḥ kaścit ko 'py udeti yathā tathā // [AgMsv_2.139]

plain_english: The bodily absorption whose nature is delight and melting is, in the unsurpassed teaching, the seal that has taken the whole world as its seal.
sanskrit_cite:
śarīragaḥ samāveśo modanadrāvaṇātmakaḥ /
sā svīkṛtajaganmudrā mudrā nairuttare mate // [AgMsv_2.140]

plain_english: This rare method of yoga abides in the heart of someone whose wheel of consciousness becomes clear, quickly, as in the case of one who is in his final birth.
sanskrit_cite:
eṣa yogavidhiḥ ko 'pi kasyāpi hṛdi vartate /
yasya prasīdec ciccakraṃ drāg apaścimajanmanaḥ // [AgMsv_2.141]

plain_english: Even while being seen by people and remaining in the condition of bodily bondage, when yoga has matured he attains in an instant an incomparable awareness.
sanskrit_cite:
lokenālokyamāno 'pi dehabandhavidhau sthitaḥ /
abhyeti yoge rūḍhe na kṣaṇāt kām api saṃvidam // [AgMsv_2.142]

plain_english: But right here, the intellect of our earlier teachers strongly affirmed the non-presence of the delusions of worldly experience.
sanskrit_cite:
atraiva tv asmatpūrvācāryāṇāṃ dhiṣaṇā bhṛśam /
abhyamaṃsta bhavābhogavibhramāṇām asaṃnidhim // [AgMsv_2.143]

plain_english: Enough with the Vedic, Samkhya, dualist, logical, Buddhist, and worldly views, and with Pancaratra, ritual scriptures, Siddhanta, and the rest.
sanskrit_cite:
vedasāṃkhyabhavedvādanyāyasaugatalaukikaiḥ /
pañcarātrakriyāśāstrasiddhāntādibhir alam // [AgMsv_2.144]

plain_english: All those various practitioners, cultivating the fitting portions of knowledge and action and established in their own procedures, act according to what is appropriate for them.
sanskrit_cite:
ucitocitavijñānakriyāṃśaparibhāvakaiḥ /
sarvaiḥ svaprakriyārūḍhais tais tair aucityayogataḥ // [AgMsv_2.145]

plain_english: Where the very extensive sequence of acts such as sowing, implanting, and digging was carried out by the many branches of the Shambhava teaching.
sanskrit_cite:
yatra bījasamāvāpakhananādikriyākramaḥ /
akāri śāmbhavānekaśākhābhir yo 'tivistṛtaḥ // [AgMsv_2.146]

plain_english: The unsurpassed fruit of that tree of consciousness-Bhairava is this, beyond practices such as life-stage observances and even ascetic marks like matted hair and ointments.
sanskrit_cite:
tasya cidbhairavataroḥ phalam etad anuttaram /
āśramasthitacaryādyair jaṭājālāñjanāntakaiḥ // [AgMsv_2.147]

plain_english: Where no difference is found between what is done and what is not done, for those who rest in that very yoga the pageantry of worldly existence dissolves.
sanskrit_cite:
kṛtair apy akṛtair vāpi yatra no labhyate bhidā /
tatraiva yoge viśrāntiṃ kurvatāṃ bhavaḍambaraḥ // [AgMsv_2.148]

plain_english: Like a mass of snow in the great summer, it melts away by itself; for when this juicy nectar of awareness is savored, that is enough.
sanskrit_cite:
himānīva mahāgrīṣme svayam eva pralīyate /
alaṃ hi carvyamāṇe 'smin sarase saṃvidāsave // [AgMsv_2.149]

plain_english: Great raptures flow forth, of which there is no number; their manifestations were already set out at length before, but here in Abhinavagupta's treatment only some are definitively stated.
sanskrit_cite:
nissaranti mahollāsāḥ saṃkhyā yeṣu na vidyate /
teṣāṃ ca prakaṭīkārāḥ kṛtāḥ prāg eva vistarāt /
atrābhinavagupte tu tattve ke 'py eva niścitāḥ // [AgMsv_2.150]

plain_english: In the rich fragrance of the ketaki flower, the bee alone is the connoisseur, not the fly; likewise, in the worship of the supreme nondual Bhairava, some rare one delights, not one deluded by duality.
sanskrit_cite:
ketakīkusumasaurabhe bhṛśaṃ \ \ bhṛṅga eva rasiko na makṣikā /
bhairavīyaparamādvayārcane \ \ ko 'pi rajyati na bhedamohitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.151]

plain_english: For one established here, no purification of any kind would need to be done anywhere; for what in the world, whose very nature is Bhairava, could be impure?
sanskrit_cite:
nātra rūḍhasya kāryā syāc chuddhiḥ kācana kutracit /
aśuddhaṃ hi jagaty eva bhairavātmani kiṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_2.152]

plain_english: And even if the mass of beings were impure, by what means could purification be effected? In that way there would be infinite regress and likewise a futile mutual dependence.
sanskrit_cite:
aśuddhe 'pi ca bhūtaughe kena śuddhiḥ pratāyatām /
anavasthā bhaved itthaṃ vyarthānyonyāśritis tathā // [AgMsv_2.153]

plain_english: When the impure is concealed, what is called the pure dissolves as well; for that is constituted by its opposite and is not established by its own nature, like blue.
sanskrit_cite:
aśuddhasya tirodhāne śuddhaṃ nāma pralīyate /
pratiyogikṛtaṃ tad dhi na svabhāvena nīlavat // [AgMsv_2.154]

plain_english: Therefore there is no insistence at all on either grasping or rejecting sense objects; for one whose nature is the consciousness of supreme Bhairava, enjoyership surges forth by itself.
sanskrit_cite:
ata eva na kaścid āgraho \ \ viṣayāṇāṃ grahaṇe 'py apohane /
parabhairavasaṃvidātmanaḥ \ \ svayam evocchalitā hi bhoktṛtā // [AgMsv_2.155]

plain_english: Since everything established here fits together by this path, the whole system is coherent. If one rejects this path, surely no other approach attains any coherence at all.
sanskrit_cite:
sarvam atra vihitaṃ yato 'munā \ \ vartmanā sakalam eva yujyate /
mārgam evam apahastya kiṃcana \ \ kāpi naiva nanu yāti yuktatām // [AgMsv_2.156]

plain_english: For example, initiation is that which cuts away impurities; but how can this possibly be explained in the view of those who assert difference?
sanskrit_cite:
tathāhi dīkṣā nāmeyaṃ yā malānāṃ nikartanī /
sa bhedavādināṃ pakṣe kathaṃ nāmopapadyate // [AgMsv_2.157]

plain_english: For how can the so-called impurity cover a self whose nature is consciousness? And where is there any act of covering for an all-pervading being?
sanskrit_cite:
tathāhi yo malo nāma sa kathaṃ citsvabhāvakam /
ātmānam āvṛṇīte kva vibhor āvaraṇakriyā // [AgMsv_2.158]

plain_english: Light is never covered by darkness, because the very arising of light is an act that destroys darkness.
sanskrit_cite:
na ca prakāśas tamasā jātu saṃvriyate yataḥ /
prakāśodaya evāyaṃ dhvāntadhvaṃsakriyātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_2.159]

plain_english: Moreover, covering is said to be an obstruction of something that moves, like rays; so how could that apply to an all-pervading being that has no motion?
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ cāvaraṇam uktaṃ hi raśmyāder gatidharmiṇaḥ /
pratīghātātmakaṃ tat kiṃ vibhor agatidharmiṇaḥ // [AgMsv_2.160]

plain_english: Or else, covering is merely the concealment of knowability, as when a pot is covered by a cloth; it is not an alteration of its own nature.
sanskrit_cite:
api vā jñeyatāmātratirodhānaṃ hi saṃvṛteḥ /
paṭādinā ghaṭādeḥ syān na svarūpānyathāsthitiḥ // [AgMsv_2.161]

plain_english: But selves, because they are of the nature of consciousness, do not admit knowability; so to speak of their being covered is not fitting even in words.
sanskrit_cite:
na cātmānaś cidātmatvāj jñeyatvam adhiśerate /
tadāvaraṇam eṣāṃ tu śabdeṣv api na śobhate // [AgMsv_2.162]

plain_english: But surely, one objects, those atomic selves are knowable to the Lord. How so? For what is of the nature of consciousness is not knowable, since that would conceal its conscious nature.
sanskrit_cite:
nanv īśvarasya te jñeyā aṇavaḥ katham īdṛśam /
cidātmakaṃ hi na jñeyaṃ cidātmatvatirohiteḥ // [AgMsv_2.163]

plain_english: The expression 'awareness is knowable' seems to recall its own fellow, the statement 'my mother is barren,' since both are self-contradictory.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃvij jñeyeti śabdo 'yaṃ vandhyā me jananītyadaḥ /
vākyaṃ smarayatīva svaṃ svātmasabrahmacāri yat // [AgMsv_2.164]

plain_english: Moreover, the Lord's omniscience would be impaired to that extent, because he would not know the covered atomic selves; yet there would be no harm to the selves themselves.
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃceśvarasya sārvajñyaṃ tāvatā pratihanyate /
āvṛtān vetti nāṇūn yan na tv eṣāṃ kācana kṣatiḥ // [AgMsv_2.165]

plain_english: But surely, when a blue object is uncovered the knower sees it, and when it is covered there is no seeing; likewise, one might say, an omniscient being covered by impurity would be obstructed.
sanskrit_cite:
nanv anāvaraṇe nīle jñātur āvaraṇe sati /
na darśanaṃ tathā bādhā na sarvajño malāvṛtaḥ // [AgMsv_2.166]

plain_english: Not so. In that case, a cloth obstructs the outgoing rays of sight, but there is no possibility of covering the knower himself.
sanskrit_cite:
maivaṃ tatra hi dṛgraśmīn gacchataḥ pratihanti tat /
paṭādi na tu vijñātur asty āvaraṇasaṃbhavaḥ // [AgMsv_2.167]

plain_english: It is clear that a non-pervading impurity cannot be the coverer of what is all-pervading; even in a pot, it would by its own nature make space non-empty only in a limited way.
sanskrit_cite:
malaś cāvyāpako vyāptur āvāraka iti sphuṭam /
ghaṭe 'pi vyomni saṃdadhyād aśūnyatvaṃ svarūpataḥ // [AgMsv_2.168]

plain_english: And if impurity produces no effect because the self is not subject to modification, how can it be capable of covering? Surely, sir, what then?
sanskrit_cite:
ātmanaś cādhikāryatvān malaḥ kiṃcitkaro na cet /
katham āvaraṇāyaiṣa śakto nanu ca bhoḥ kimu // [AgMsv_2.169]

plain_english: Indeed, its covering is said to be merely the existence of impurity; the atomic self is described as covered simply because it has impurity as a second.
sanskrit_cite:
malasadbhāvamātraṃ hi tasyāvaraṇam ucyate /
malena sadvitīyo 'ṇur āvṛtaḥ paribhāṣyate // [AgMsv_2.170]

plain_english: Alas, by this reasoning, even for those of the stated nature there would truly be a covering of Shiva, merely from the existence of impurity.
sanskrit_cite:
hantānena nayenaiṣa śivam uktātmanām api /
sthitam āvaraṇaṃ satyaṃ malasadbhāvamātrataḥ // [AgMsv_2.171]

plain_english: Moreover, if the self covered by impurity does not even know the impurity, then in that non-awareness of it, is another impurity to be posited?
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃcāvṛto malenātmā malam eva na vetti kim /
tadasaṃvedane tasya kiṃ malāntaram ucyate // [AgMsv_2.172]

plain_english: But what of it? Let it know the impurity. Then, without vidya and kala, there would be omniscience; and if the impurity were known, the self could abandon it by various contrived means.
sanskrit_cite:
nanv ataḥ kiṃ malaṃ vettu tarhi vidyākale vinā /
sarvajñatvaṃ bhavet tac ca malaṃ viditam eva sat // [AgMsv_2.173]

plain_english: Let the self abandon it by those various contrived means; and if so, what covering would that impurity produce in the self?
sanskrit_cite:
jahātv ātmābhyupāyais tais tair vicitraiḥ prakalpitaiḥ /
kiṃcāvaraṇam etena yasyātmani bhavet tataḥ // [AgMsv_2.174]

plain_english: How would this self come to be a knower and doer with respect to pots and such things? Surely, one replies, because vidya and kala are held to be the basis of limited knowing and doing.
sanskrit_cite:
ghaṭādau jñātṛkartṛtve katham asya bhaviṣyataḥ /
nanu vidyākale kiṃcijjñatvakartṛtvapade smṛte // [AgMsv_2.175]

plain_english: In this way the deluded are deceived, but not the wise: this maya is inert by nature, and kala and the rest are its offspring.
sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ vimūḍhamatayo vañcyante na tu paṇḍitāḥ /
jaḍasvabhāvā māyaiṣā tatsūtiś ca kalādikaḥ // [AgMsv_2.176]

plain_english: How could what is non-conscious be capable of manifesting consciousness? And if all-pervading consciousness were manifested, how could it be qualified by limitedness and such attributes?
sanskrit_cite:
acidātmā kathaṃkāraṃ cidabhivyañjanakṣamaḥ /
abhivyaktā ca cidvibhvī kiṃcittvādiviśeṣaṇaiḥ // [AgMsv_2.177]

plain_english: How could it become qualified? For that is fitting only for things that have parts. But surely, one objects, God, using kala and vidya, could manifest consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
viśeṣyatāṃ kathaṃ nāma sāṃśavastūcitaṃ hi tat /
nanu devaḥ kalāvidyākaraṇo vyañjayec citam // [AgMsv_2.178]

plain_english: Let him manifest it in all ways—alas, there is no incapacity in him. But if there is insistence on an eternal impurity, how will liberation ever come about?
sanskrit_cite:
vyanaktu sarvato hanta nāsyāśaktir athāgrahaḥ /
male sadātane cāsya kathaṃ muktir bhaviṣyati // [AgMsv_2.179]

plain_english: The claim that impurity has an obstructing power which sometimes stops and sometimes acts is foolish talk.
sanskrit_cite:
roddhrī śaktir malasyāsti sā ca kvāpi nivartate /
kvāpi pravartate ceti dhig idaṃ mūḍhabhāṣitam // [AgMsv_2.180]

plain_english: Insentient things cannot deliberate, so how could that selective operation happen? If so, one must admit that God is the cause even in that case.
sanskrit_cite:
jaḍānāṃ ko 'nusandhiḥ syāt taṃ vinaitat kathaṃ bhavet /
atha tatrāpi devasya hetutābhyupagamyate // [AgMsv_2.181]

plain_english: For what reason would that God set that power in motion, or for what reason would he make it stop again once it has been set in motion?
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ nimittam asau devas tāṃ śaktiṃ saṃpravartayet /
pravartitāṃ vā kiṃ nāma tāṃ nivartayate punaḥ // [AgMsv_2.182]

plain_english: If the answer is that God acts from autonomy, then let that plenitude alone be accepted. Why bring in impurity, which is of the nature of darkness, and why suppose any maturation of it at all?
sanskrit_cite:
svātantryād iti cet pūrṇaṃ tad evāśrīyate na kim /
malasya dhvāntarūpasya na ca pāko 'pi kaścana // [AgMsv_2.183]

plain_english: For maturation, by involving a connection with another state, would destroy mala's fixed nature. By this reasoning, the idea that a soul is impelled by God's will because of its connection with impurity is refuted.
sanskrit_cite:
sa hy anyatādānayogād dhanty amuṣya dhruvātmatām /
etena malasaṃbandhād īśvarecchāpracoditaḥ // [AgMsv_2.184]

plain_english: The claim that the bound soul, caught up in the desire for enjoyment, is favored by creation is struck at the root; that consequence follows from what has been shown.
sanskrit_cite:
bhogalobhakathāviṣṭaḥ paśuḥ sṛṣṭyānugṛhyate /
iti yad bhaṇyate mūlahataṃ taj, janitaṃ tataḥ // [AgMsv_2.185]

plain_english: They know impurity to be nothing but the mere play of concealing one's own self. For why would the autonomous, all-pervading Lord not manifest anything within himself?
sanskrit_cite:
svātmapracchādanakrīḍāmātram eva malaṃ viduḥ /
svatantro hi vibhuḥ kiṃcit kiṃ na svātmani bhāsayet // [AgMsv_2.186]

plain_english: And as for karma, which is also accepted, let that first be examined. For even if the connection with karma remains, how can there be such a state as the great dissolution?
sanskrit_cite:
yac ca karmāpi nāmeṣṭaṃ tattāvat pravicāryatām /
tathāhi karmasaṃbandhe sthite 'pi katham īdṛśaḥ // [AgMsv_2.187]

plain_english: How can there be a great dissolution, or a great creation? Surely, one may say, karma becomes restrained there by the will of God.
sanskrit_cite:
mahāpralaya ucyate mahāsṛṣṭiś ca vā katham /
nanv īśvarecchayā tatra karmāyāti niruddhatām // [AgMsv_2.188]

plain_english: Does the Lord do this through karma's inactivity, or by depending on another karma, or not? In the first alternative, that very possibility becomes an issue.
sanskrit_cite:
karmaudāsīnyayogena karmāntaram apekṣatām /
īśvaro 'tha navā pūrvapakṣe saṃbhava eva ca // [AgMsv_2.189]

plain_english: If that is impossible, in what respect could he possess sovereignty? Then all this—creation, dissolution, and the rest—would come about from karma alone.
sanskrit_cite:
nasaṃbhave sa kutrāṃśe caiśvaryam adhigacchatu /
karmataḥ sarvam evedaṃ syāt sṛṣṭipralayādikam // [AgMsv_2.190]

plain_english: But if, without depending on karma, he restrains karmas, then let the all-pervading Lord keep them restrained always.
sanskrit_cite:
atha karmānapekṣo vā karmaṇāṃ rodhanaṃ tataḥ /
sadā niruddhāny eveśaḥ karmāṇi kurutāṃ vibhuḥ // [AgMsv_2.191]

plain_english: But surely their nature is to produce enjoyment. How could that be an intrinsic nature if it has come to depend on another condition?
sanskrit_cite:
nanu teṣāṃ svabhāvo 'yaṃ yadbhogaprasavātmatā /
kathaṃ svabhāva eṣa syād yaḥ paropādhitāṃ gataḥ // [AgMsv_2.192]

plain_english: For the intrinsic nature of things is independent. Therefore, whatever form karmas have when they do not depend on the Lord's direction—that is their own true nature.
sanskrit_cite:
anapekṣo hi bhāvānāṃ svabhāvaḥ karmaṇāṃ tataḥ /
īśaiṣaṇānapekṣāṇāṃ yadrūpaṃ tatsvakaṃ vapuḥ // [AgMsv_2.193]

plain_english: And do the karmas dissolved in the great dissolution, or even those that still persist, get awakened by God? What, indeed, is accomplished by those karmas?
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ ca pralayalīnāni karmāṇi sthitibhāñjy api /
kiṃ prabodhayate devaḥ kiṃ nu dṛ[sṛ]ṣṭair hi taiḥ kṛtam // [AgMsv_2.194]

plain_english: If it is said to be for the maturation of impurity, that too has been thoroughly dismissed. And this self is all-pervading—what, indeed, can karma do to it?
sanskrit_cite:
malapākāya cet so 'pi sudūram apasāritaḥ /
kiṃ cātmā vibhur evaiṣa sa kiṃ nāma karoti hi // [AgMsv_2.195]

plain_english: This examination has already been elaborated at length. In the clay, stick, wheel, and threads, it is the intelligent Lord who stands as the true agent.
sanskrit_cite:
iti pūrvaṃ vicāraś ca vistareṇa prapañcitaḥ /
mṛddaṇḍacakrasūtreṣu dhīmān karteśvaraḥ sthitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.196]

plain_english: In what respect, indeed, does the potter's agency stand, especially in the sprouting and growth of seeds that have not been ploughed or cultivated?
sanskrit_cite:
kumbhakārasya kartṛtvaṃ kutrāṃśe nv avatiṣṭhatām /
akṛṣṭapacyabījeṣu prarohaprasavādike // [AgMsv_2.197]

plain_english: Let it be a cause earlier, but not in the crops—what principle is that? This is a bad deed and that a good deed, distinguished by the difference in their fruits.
sanskrit_cite:
pūrvaṃ karotu hetutvaṃ na sasyeṣv iti ko nayaḥ /
idaṃ duṣkṛtam etac ca sukṛtaṃ phalabhedataḥ // [AgMsv_2.198]

plain_english: If that division is made, does only his will unfold there? If he is autonomous, why would he adopt a will of his own that causes harm to others?
sanskrit_cite:
iti yat pravibhaktaṃ kiṃ tatrāsyecchaiva jṛmbhate /
svatantro yady asau kasmāt parapīḍākārīṃ nijām // [AgMsv_2.199]

plain_english: Why would he, who is always filled with compassion, adopt such a will? But surely, one may say, karma is such by its own nature and therefore gives those fruits.
sanskrit_cite:
icchāṃ gṛhṇāti yo nityaṃ karuṇārasanirbharaḥ /
nanu svabhāvāttattādṛk karmātaḥ phaladāyakam // [AgMsv_2.200]

plain_english: Considering that karma might be pacified through expiation and the like, God accordingly promulgates scripture that gives varied instruction.
sanskrit_cite:
prāyaścittādikaraṇāc chāmyec ceti vicārayan /
devas tathaiva tanute śāstraṃ citropadeśakam // [AgMsv_2.201]

plain_english: To say that the Śaiva teaching, or that karmas, are such by their own nature—what principle is that? People like us know that a seed has the nature of producing a sprout.
sanskrit_cite:
śaivaṃ, svabhāva edādṛk karmaṇām iti ko nayaḥ /
bījam aṅkurasaṃsūtisvabhāvam iti mādṛśaḥ // [AgMsv_2.202]

plain_english: People like us are able to know such things from the established usage of earlier generations. But the Lord, indeed, never acts without his own will.
sanskrit_cite:
pūrvavṛddhavyavahṛter vijñātuṃ prabhaviṣṇavaḥ /
īśvaras tu nijecchayā vinā na hi kadācana // [AgMsv_2.203]

plain_english: Having observed the intricate diversity of karmic fruits, if the Lord alone were the doer of everything, the group of individual selves could in no way be doers. But if they too are not doers, then, aiming at these beings barren of action, the Lord would not be the all-doer.
sanskrit_cite:
avalokitavān karmaphalavaicitryacāturīm /

tasmād devaḥ sarvakartā yadi syāt kartāraḥ syur nātmavargāḥ kathaṃcid /
no kartāras te 'pi cet karmavandhyān uddiśyainān sarvakartā na devaḥ // [AgMsv_2.204]

plain_english: Thus, from the standpoint of duality, this so-called karma is not well-reasoned. Here only a brief summary is given, while the fuller elaboration has been shown elsewhere.
sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ ca bhedadṛṣṭyedaṃ karma nāma na mu[yu]ktimat /
etāvān atra saṃkṣopo vyāso 'nyatra tu darśitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.205]

plain_english: The Lord is one, whose very nature is consciousness; therefore he is indeed the all-doer by his own nature. Because of diversity, he is spoken of as connected with karma.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃvedanātmako deva ekas tasmāt svataḥ khalu /
sarvakartā sa vaicitryāt karmayogīti bhaṇyate // [AgMsv_2.206]

plain_english: And that so-called Maya, which is established as the cause of the universe, containing within her womb the elements of the tattvas ending with earth—if she is clearly eternal...
sanskrit_cite:
māyā ca nāma viśvasya yā kāraṇam iti sthitā /
sā dharaṇyantatattvāṃśagarbhā nityā yadi sphuṭam // [AgMsv_2.207]

plain_english: Then dissolution would never occur. But surely it occurs through the state of manifestation? We do not recognize manifestation as such, because cognition consists in being an object of grasping.
sanskrit_cite:
pralayo na kadācit syān nanu sa vyaktibhāvataḥ /
vyaktiṃ nāma na jānīmo vijñānaṃ grāhyatā yataḥ // [AgMsv_2.208]

plain_english: Its being grasped by the Lord's supreme knowledge is everlasting. If that were absent, how could the Lord be the cause?
sanskrit_cite:
tadīśvaraparajñānagrāhyatāsti sadātanī /
tasyām avidyamānāyām īśvaraḥ kāraṇaṃ kutaḥ // [AgMsv_2.209]

plain_english: One might think it will be in the Lord as when someone clearly produces a pot. Not so, because of the distinction between inner and outer instruments.
sanskrit_cite:
sphuṭaṃ prakurute kumbhaṃ tadvad īśe bhaviṣyati /
maivam antarbahīrūpakaraṇapravibhedataḥ // [AgMsv_2.210]

plain_english: In the making of a pot, cognition that is clear, unclear, and so forth is fitting; but the Lord possesses a clear, noble, prior cognition.
sanskrit_cite:
sphuṭāsphuṭādivijñānaṃ yuktaṃ kumbhakṛti sphuṭam /
īśvarasya sphuṭodārapūrvavijñānaśālinaḥ // [AgMsv_2.211]

plain_english: What part would not be known, even where dependence on manifestation is assumed? In the view of the satkarya theorists, the universe is clearly established even in the cause.
sanskrit_cite:
ko na jñāto bhaved bhāgo yatrāpi vyaktyapekṣitā /
satkāryavādināṃ deśe kāraṇe 'pi sphuṭaṃ sthitam // [AgMsv_2.212]

plain_english: Thus, for the universe to be clearly present in Maya would be incongruous, since Siva and the selves are pervasive, together with the tattvas and mutually so.
sanskrit_cite:
viśvam ityapi māyāyāṃ sphuṭaṃ syād asamañjasam /
vyāpakāś ca śivātmānas tattvaiḥ sākaṃ parasparam // [AgMsv_2.213]

plain_english: And how indeed could they exist, given the concealment of pervasiveness? The supreme expansion of consciousness is its pervasion, and in division it is spoken of accordingly.
sanskrit_cite:
kathaṃ ca nāma vidyantāṃ vyāpakatvatirohiteḥ /
vikāsaḥ paramo vyāptiḥ saṃvido bheda ucyate // [AgMsv_2.214]

plain_english: The group of coverings born of Maya, as well as the collection of instruments, has already been examined before, and the group of effects has also been discussed.
sanskrit_cite:
māyīyaṃ kañcukavrātaṃ yathā karaṇasaṃcayaḥ /
vicāritaḥ pūrvam eva kāryavargaś ca carcitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.215]

plain_english: As long as the universe, devoid of resting on the state of Siva, does not shine forth, this is merely talk of its autonomy; let that be understood.
sanskrit_cite:
yāvac chivapadādhyāsavandhyaṃ viśvaṃ na visphuret /
tatsvātantryakathāmātram etad ity avadhāryatām // [AgMsv_2.216]

plain_english: Thus, in the absence of impurity and the like, what initiation could there be, who would be the initiator, and who the recipient? None of this fits.
sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ malādyabhāve hi kā dīkṣā ko hi dīkṣakaḥ /
dīkṣāpātraṃ ca ko vā syād iti kiṃcin na yujyate // [AgMsv_2.217]

plain_english: How could the installation of the entire path in the disciple, the path, the fire, the vessel, the mandala, the ladle, the hand, and so on, be possible?
sanskrit_cite:
śiṣye 'dhvany anale kumbhe maṇḍale srukkarādike /
samastādhvakṛto nyāsaḥ kathaṃ vāpy upapadyatām // [AgMsv_2.218]

plain_english: Surely they would not all be present in that way. But, one may object, by the power of conception this entire relation of purifier and purified has indeed been declared.
sanskrit_cite:
nahi tāvanta eva syur nanu saṃkalpanāvaśāt /
śodhyaśodhakabhāvo 'yaṃ sarva evodito nanu // [AgMsv_2.219]

plain_english: If what is merely imagined could bear fruit, then truly those who have gained riches in the kingdom of fantasy would triumph by attaining the repose of heavenly sovereignty.
sanskrit_cite:
kalpitaṃ cet phalet satyaṃ manorājyārjitaśriyaḥ /
jayanti nākasāmrājyalābhaviśrāntiyogataḥ // [AgMsv_2.220]

plain_english: Do states that follow the path of strong, vivid conception not bear fruit in that way, like the destruction of poison through meditation and the like?
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ nāma balavadrūpasaṃkalpapathavartinaḥ /
phalanti na tathā bhāvā dhyānādiviṣanāśavat // [AgMsv_2.221]

plain_english: Meditation is precisely firmness of conception; but meditation tainted by doubt does not bear fruit at all, because it grasps two alternatives.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃkalpadārḍhyam ity eva dhyānaṃ saṃśayarūṣitam /
dhyānaṃ ca na phaled eva svayaṃ pakṣadvayāgrahāt // [AgMsv_2.222]

plain_english: Look—if its fruit were to arise from the application of conception, why would you desire some external entities that are not made of consciousness?
sanskrit_cite:
hanta saṃkalpanāyogād yadi jāyeta tatphalam /
kim asaṃvinmayān bhāvān bāhyān kāṃścit abhīpsasi // [AgMsv_2.223]

plain_english: By conception alone there is consecration pertaining to the pit, fire, guru, and disciple; and that same thing, appearing as the fruit, remains as that consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃkalpenaiva saṃskāraḥ kuṇḍāgniguruśiṣyagaḥ /
sa eva ca phalābhāsī tatsaṃvid avaśiṣyate // [AgMsv_2.224]

plain_english: And the manifestation in such a form of autonomous consciousness should indeed be understood as initiation, by which beings are liberated.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃvidaś ca svatantrāyās tathārūpāvabhāsanam /
dīkṣeti kila mantavyaṃ muñcyante jantavo yayā // [AgMsv_2.225]

plain_english: For that very reason, no sequence or fixed rule has been determined here in the scripture regarding the essential nature, taking, or measure of sesame, ghee, and the like.
sanskrit_cite:
ata eva tilājyādeḥ svarūpe grahaṇe mitau /
kramo vā niyamo neha kaścic chāstre nirūpitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.226]

plain_english: But surely, what fixed rule is there in mantras? For the supreme form is declared to partake of all letters; so how could initiation not be the same way?
sanskrit_cite:
nanu mantreṣu kiṃ nāma niyamaḥ sarvavarṇabhāk /
rūpaṃ paraṃ hi kathitaṃ dīkṣāpi na tathā katham // [AgMsv_2.227]

plain_english: Thus, the burning of letters as you approve it is indeed beneficial; but for those who have not yet attained firm establishment, a definite rule certainly applies to them.
sanskrit_cite:
evam evārṇadāhasya yadbhavatsaṃmataṃ hitam /
kiṃ tu tāvati ye rūḍhiṃ na prāptās tān prati dhruvam // [AgMsv_2.228]

plain_english: This mantric rule has been declared and it serves a real purpose, for those mantras are awakened and move along the path of reflective awareness.
sanskrit_cite:
māntro 'yaṃ niyamaḥ prokta upayogaṃ ca gacchati /
pratibuddhā hi te mantrā vimarśapathavartinaḥ // [AgMsv_2.229]

plain_english: Because the light of consciousness is autonomous, the mantras, made of agency, enter that very teacher through the application of identity with it.
sanskrit_cite:
svatantrasyaiva ciddhāmna svātantryāt kartṛtāmayāḥ /
mantrā viśanty evācāryaṃ taṃ tādātmyaniyogataḥ // [AgMsv_2.230]

plain_english: They make him autonomous, and even instruments attain agency; thus, initiation and whatever other rites are accepted become possible.
sanskrit_cite:
svatantrīkurvate yānti karaṇāny api kartṛtām /
itthaṃ dīkṣādividhaye ye 'py anye vidhayo matāḥ // [AgMsv_2.231]

plain_english: What, indeed, is to be done by those who act, and how could there even be prohibition? Both are established right here, for all of that is enjoined here.
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ nāma kurvatāṃ kṛtyaṃ niṣedhaṃ tv api vā katham /
te 'py atraivopapadyante tat sarvaṃ vihitaṃ tv iha // [AgMsv_2.232]

plain_english: And all this is prohibited only from that other standpoint; for when its prohibition is clearly shown, what force does it have for one who rests on the nondual path?
sanskrit_cite:
sarvaṃ caitad amutraiva pratiṣiddhaṃ yataḥ sphuṭam /
pratiṣedhe darśite 'sya kiṃ cādvaitapathāśritaḥ // [AgMsv_2.233]

plain_english: Even prohibition is enjoined, and that too is prohibited; thus the ocean of one's own awareness surges abundantly within itself.
sanskrit_cite:
pratiṣedho 'pi vihitaḥ so 'pi ca pratiṣidhyate /
itthaṃ svasaṃvidambhodhiḥ svātmani procchalaty alam // [AgMsv_2.234]

plain_english: Thus this entire universe is beautiful with the bliss of the world, and in this way it utterly dissolves the opposing element of difference.
sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ ca viśvam evedaṃ jagadānandasundaram /
tadvipakṣaṃ ca bhedāṃśam itthaṃ kṣapayatetarām // [AgMsv_2.235]

plain_english: From the moon of knowledge risen from the mouth of the Supreme Lord, beautiful rays radiant with the fullness of their own light spread in all directions.
sanskrit_cite:
parameśamukhodbhūtajñānacandrasya sarvataḥ /
tāvatā svaprabhābhārabhāsvarāḥ sumarīcayaḥ // [AgMsv_2.236]

plain_english: The deadly poison that darkens the moon of all beings, melted by the mere touch of the mass of rays from Shiva's moon, turns into an elixir.
sanskrit_cite:
śivacandrāṃśusaṃghātapātamātravilāpitaḥ /
samastabhāvaśītāṃśukālakūṭo rasāyate // [AgMsv_2.237]

plain_english: Plunging there unceasingly and reeling from drinking that essence, we become that essence itself and abide pure, freed from the three kinds of suffering.
sanskrit_cite:
tatrāniśaṃ nimajjantas tadrasāpānaghūrṇitāḥ /
tadrasībhūya tiṣṭhāmaḥ śuddhās tāpatrayojjhitāḥ // [AgMsv_2.238]

plain_english: The mouth of the Supreme Lord is said to be his power, namely will; having arisen, that will takes on the functioning of the moon of knowledge in the distinct states beginning with Īśvara.
sanskrit_cite:
parameśamukhaṃ tu śaktir uktā bhavatīcchā nanu sodbhavaṃ gatā /
pratipadyata īśvarādibhinnasthitivijñānaśaśāṅkaśaktivṛttam // [AgMsv_2.239]

plain_english: The fully spread mass of rays streaming forth on all sides from that moon is indeed the Supreme Lord's own power, declared to consist of action and to be made of the world.
sanskrit_cite:
śaśinaḥ kila tasya sarvato yaḥ paripūrṇaḥ prasṛto marīcipuñjaḥ /
iyam eva hi sā kriyātmikoktā parameśasya jaganmayī svaśaktiḥ // [AgMsv_2.240]

plain_english: Thus this, full of the three powers, expands as the supreme Bhairava alone; nothing different from it could exist, and its own expansion is proclaimed as its victory.
sanskrit_cite:
tad idaṃ trikaśaktinirbharaṃ paramaṃ bhairavam eva jṛmbhate /
na tu tadvyatireki saṃbhavet svavijṛmbhā vijayo 'sya kīrtitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.241]

plain_english: From that very reality these powers clearly conquer the world; the meaning becomes manifest and fits for us, since such a connection with many expressions belongs to that fullness and accommodates the division of statements.
sanskrit_cite:
tata eva jagaj jayanty amī sphuṭam arthaḥ prakaṭo 'pi yujyate naḥ /
bahuvācakayoga īdṛśaṃ tat paripūrṇatvam amuṣya vākyabhedam // [AgMsv_2.242]

plain_english: Thus this single verse clearly explains Bhairava himself, whose nature is consciousness, full of the entire sequence of all beings.
sanskrit_cite:
ity eka eva śloko 'yaṃ cidātmā bhairavaḥ svayam /
samastabhāvasaṃdarbhanirbharo vyākṛtaḥ sphuṭam // [AgMsv_2.243]

plain_english: For the destruction of the poison of worldly existence, those whose vision is empowered by Garuda employ poison itself and attain an immortal state.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃsāragaranāśāya tārkṣyādhiṣṭhitadṛṣṭayaḥ /
viṣam evopayuñjānāḥ prāpnuvanty amṛtīṃ sthitim // [AgMsv_2.244]

plain_english: Thus it has been shown to this extent: by self-luminous own-awareness everything is established, and apart from that nothing at all is possible.
sanskrit_cite:
iti darśitam etāvat svaprakāśasvasaṃvidā /
siddhaṃ tadvyatirekeṇa na kiṃcid eva kalpate // [AgMsv_2.245]

plain_english: Whatever rests in own-awareness is real to that very extent; for if reality depended on another time, it could not be real anywhere.
sanskrit_cite:
yāvatsvasaṃvidviśrāntaṃ yat tāvat tat sad eva hi /
kālāntaravyapekṣe hi satyatvaṃ syān na kutracit // [AgMsv_2.246]

plain_english: The connection of awareness with time has been refuted at length; therefore own-awareness functions just as it spreads out space.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃvidaḥ kālayogaś ca vistareṇa nivāritaḥ /
tat svasaṃvid yathā deśaṃ vitared vartate tathā // [AgMsv_2.247]

plain_english: Likewise, whatever cannot be placed on the touchstone of awareness is fit only for doubt; even in scripture that is called unreal.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā saṃvidy akṣamayyāṃ nikaṣāśmani ropitam /
na yat tat saṃśayāyaiva śāstre 'py uktam avastu tat // [AgMsv_2.248]

plain_english: What does not rise to own-awareness is no different from idle talk; that alone is scripture and that alone is method which unfolds within awareness.
sanskrit_cite:
svasaṃvid anupārohi pralāpān na viśiṣyate /
tac cchāstraṃ prakriyā sā ca yat saṃvidi vivartate // [AgMsv_2.249]

plain_english: All these risings and settings of the whole world arise from the heart, like a dream from deep sleep, and are examined by the scripture of own-awareness.
sanskrit_cite:
hṛdayāj jagato jātāḥ sarvasyaite kṣayodayāḥ /
svapnasyeva suṣuptākhyāt svasaṃvicchāstracarcitāḥ // [AgMsv_2.250]

plain_english: The totality of form, light, and attention; withdrawal, maintenance, and creation; closing and opening; and the construction of contraction in beings — all these are its operations.
sanskrit_cite:
rūpālokamanaskārasāmagrī saṃhṛtiḥ sthitiḥ /
sṛṣṭir nimeṣonmeṣau ca satāṃ saṃkocakalpanam // [AgMsv_2.251]

plain_english: Such an abiding state, having the form of knower, known, and knowing, is always the spontaneous fashioning of the manifold world by perfectly full own-consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
ityādikā mātṛmeyamānarūpā sthitiḥ sadā /
svasaṃvidaḥ supūrṇāyāḥ prapañcaracanā svayam // [AgMsv_2.252]

plain_english: She indeed is by herself the form of all, of all selves, directions, places, and times; and from her alone arises the determination of what is true and what is false.
sanskrit_cite:
sarvasarvātmadigdeśakālākārā svayaṃ hi sā /
satyamithyātvanirṇītis tata eva hi jāyate // [AgMsv_2.253]

plain_english: Teacher Utpaladeva also taught this very thing: even what appears outside as being or nonbeing is, in own-consciousness, my seeing.
sanskrit_cite:
ācāryotpaladevo 'pi tadetadupadiṣṭavān /
bahiḥ sadasadātmāpi svasaṃvidi madīyadṛk // [AgMsv_2.254]

plain_english: The regulation of the autonomous, expressed as 'let it see' and called together with the senses, is that very consciousness which, ascending from Shiva down to the worm, rests upon its own awareness.
sanskrit_cite:
paśyatv iti svatantrasya niyatiḥ sendriyābhidhā /
saiva rūdhā śivād ā ca krimeḥ svāṃ saṃvidaṃ śritā // [AgMsv_2.255]

plain_english: That very same reality is worldly bondage, and it is Shiva, the supreme lord; one who has attained rest in it is called liberated.
sanskrit_cite:
tad eva deve saṃsāraḥ sa śivaḥ parameīŭvaraḥ /
tatra viśrāntim āpanno mukta ity abhidhīyate // [AgMsv_2.256]

plain_english: By the grace of this, all beings from Brahma down to the immobile live; let this consciousness be understood as always unobscured.
sanskrit_cite:
etatprasādāj jīvanti brahmādyāḥ sthāvarāntakāḥ /
aviluptā sadā seyaṃ saṃvittir iti gṛhyatām // [AgMsv_2.257]

plain_english: Even while shining forth, that goddess never establishes a self anywhere as devoid of her; in one place she may establish it, in another fault it, in another do otherwise.
sanskrit_cite:
vibhānty api hi sā devī na tayā rahitaṃ kvacit /
ātmānaṃ sādhayet kvāpi kvāpi dūṣayate kvacit // [AgMsv_2.258]

plain_english: She places things otherwise, yet she does not undergo change; even while barren of establishing, faulting, and otherness, she remains the supreme goddess.
sanskrit_cite:
anyathaiva sthāpayate na ca yāti vikāritām /
sādhandūṣaṇānyatvavandhyāpi parameśvarī // [AgMsv_2.259]

plain_english: And she shines clearly in that very way, autonomous indeed; she is the glorious great lord, the god who is the teacher even of those who came before.
sanskrit_cite:
bhāsate ca tathātvena tat svatantrā sphuṭā hi sā /
śrīmān maheśvaro devaḥ pūrveṣām api yo guruḥ // [AgMsv_2.260]

plain_english: He proclaimed this for the grace of the world: 'Deluded ones, why do you abide in vain in essenceless speech like the cawing of crows? Honoring your own consciousness, all who respect what is instructed even nearby by the goddess-consciousness become liberated while living, in whatever place they are.'
sanskrit_cite:
sa etad eva provāca lokānugrahahetutaḥ /

mūḍhāḥ kiṃ niḥsāre vāyasaviraṭitakalpe tiṣṭatha vacasi vṛthaivaṃ svāṃ saṃvidam āvarjya /
saṃviddevatayaiva yad ādiṣṭaṃ nikaṭe 'py atha sarva ādriyamāṇās tattaddeśe jīvanmuktā bhavanti // [AgMsv_2.261]

plain_english: Therefore, in this guiding principle, consciousness alone is called the teacher, because it indeed swallows the universe through creation and dissolution.
sanskrit_cite:
tad atra nītau saṃvittir evāsau gurur ucyate /
giraty eva yato viśvaṃ sṛṣṭisaṃhṛtiyogataḥ // [AgMsv_2.262]

plain_english: Therefore, here the primary firm relation is called the supreme one; whatever knowledge is instructed through it is indeed innately accomplished.
sanskrit_cite:
tad atra mukhyā yā rūḍhiḥ saṃbandhaḥ para ucyate /
enayā yad yad ādiṣṭaṃ jñānaṃ sāṃsiddhikaṃ tu tat // [AgMsv_2.263]

plain_english: Where the eternal abiding of our lineage of teachers is established, from there proceeds the division of the transmission beginning with Tryambaka.
sanskrit_cite:
yatrāsmadguruvargasya sthitā nityāvasthitiḥ /
traiyambakādisaṃtānabhedo yasmāt pravartate // [AgMsv_2.264]

plain_english: Where it was previously said that identity with ignorance perishes, this world shines forth from the variety grasped by own-consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
yatroktaṃ pūrvam ajñānatādātmyaṃ naśyatītyapi /
svasaṃvidas tu vaicitryaṃ gṛhṇatyā bhāty ayaṃ tataḥ // [AgMsv_2.265]

plain_english: The confluence of scriptures—intermediate, great-divine, divine, and so forth—consists of the rays of the teacher's own true speech, fashioned by his own self.
sanskrit_cite:
antarālamahaddivyādivyādi śāstrasaṃgamaḥ /
tattvavannijavāgaṃśūn guror ātmavinirmitān // [AgMsv_2.266]

plain_english: The primacy of own-consciousness is manifest—whether from the teacher, from scripture, or from oneself; therefore this effort has been made with that as primary.
sanskrit_cite:
prādhānyaṃ prakaṭaṃ svasaṃvidaḥ /
gurutaḥ kila śāstrataḥ svataḥ /
tad ayaṃ mukhyatayā kṛtaḥ śramaḥ // [AgMsv_2.267]

plain_english: The teacher depends on the operation of scripture, and that is established in one's own self-consciousness; therefore all this attains accomplishment through self-consciousness and is never obstructed.
sanskrit_cite:
śāstravṛttiparatantrito guruḥ svātmasaṃvidi ca tatpratiṣṭhitam /
tena sarvam idam ātmasaṃvidā siddhim eti nahi jātv asahyatām // [AgMsv_2.268]

plain_english: O seekers of liberation, let this scripture be practiced with effort; do not let life be spent in vain, strained over other scriptures.
sanskrit_cite:
etac chāstraṃ prayatnena carcyatāṃ he mumukṣavaḥ /
mā vṛthaivāyur āyastam anyaśāstreṣu nīyatām // [AgMsv_2.269]

plain_english: Whatever view of non-difference or view of difference there may be, it comes to fulfillment here alone; therefore let this be carefully examined.
sanskrit_cite:
abhedadṛṣṭir yā kācid bhedadṛṣṭir athāpi vā /
sātraivāyāti nirvāhaṃ tenaitat pravicāryatām // [AgMsv_2.270]

plain_english: Just as one is freed from sleep by recognizing the dream state, so one whose heart is awakened by sustained practice of this scripture remains always awake.
sanskrit_cite:
svapnakālaparijñānavī[tanidro] yathā tathā /
etacchāstrasamabhyāsaprabuddhahṛdayaḥ sadā // [AgMsv_2.271]

plain_english: Own-consciousness indeed is that scripture, and she is free from dependence; if it is to be stated thus, let its authoritativeness be said to be from itself.
sanskrit_cite:
svasaṃvid eva tac chāstraṃ sā cāpekṣāvivarjitā /
tathā yady abhidhīyeta svataḥ prāmāṇyam ucyatām // [AgMsv_2.272]

plain_english: Teaching, what is to be taught, and the teacher—this triad, in that state, is not measured by time and is beautiful with freedom and nonduality.
sanskrit_cite:
śāsanaṃ śāsitavyaṃ ca śāsakaṃ ceti yat kila /
tattatrākālakalitaṃ svātantryādvaitasundaram // [AgMsv_2.273]

plain_english: Having internalized that intrinsic, never-departing state, lord Shrikantha proclaimed it in the glorious Kirana scripture.
sanskrit_cite:
tām avasthitim ātmīyāṃ garbhīkṛtyānapāyinīm /
śrīkaṇṭhanāthaḥ provāca śrīmatkiraṇaśāsane // [AgMsv_2.274]

plain_english: All this is for the sake of engaging hearers through differentiation; but this difference, arising from difference of meaning, is constructed only by metaphorical usage.
sanskrit_cite:
sarvam etat pravṛttyarthaṃ śrot\rr ṇāṃ tu vibhedataḥ /
arthabhedāt tu bhedo 'yam upacārāt prakalpate // [AgMsv_2.275]

plain_english: No difference of fruit should be assumed here in the Lord's teaching; if one were assumed, it would be a false assumption, making this teaching of the Lord appear divided by distinctions of ten, eighteen, eight, and eight.
sanskrit_cite:
phalabhedo na kalpyo 'tra kalpyaś ced ayathātatham /
daśakāṣṭādaśāṣṭāṣṭabhedabhinnam idaṃ vibhoḥ // [AgMsv_2.276]

plain_english: This teaching has the single fruit of attaining the state of being Śiva, and it applies to the qualified individual soul who is eager for that attainment, without regard for birth, family, caste, and the like.
sanskrit_cite:
śivasadbhāvalābhaikaphalaṃ tallābhaprotsuke /
adhikāriṇy aṇau jātikulavarṇādyanādarāt // [AgMsv_2.277]

plain_english: As long as this teaching, once set forth, maintains its unity of discourse, the wise know it as one, even though there is variety in the functions of its subsidiary and principal parts.
sanskrit_cite:
pravṛttam ekavākyatvaṃ yāvad āsādya vartate /
aṅgāṅgivṛttavaicitryāt tāvad ekam idaṃ viduḥ // [AgMsv_2.278]

plain_english: The Trika scripture, the teacher who is of that nature and nondual here, and the collection of its subsequent textual portions and sections all belong to the same unified framework.
sanskrit_cite:
trikaśāstraṃ tathābhūto gurur atrādvayātmakaḥ /
tadanantaravākyāṃśapuñjaḥ prakaraṇāni ca // [AgMsv_2.279]

plain_english: Even when the accounts of differences produced by māyā become clear, the attainment of Śiva remains established as the primary and final fruit.
sanskrit_cite:
māyīyabhedavṛttāntasphuṭabhāve bhavanti ca /
tathāpi śivasaṃprāptir mukhyam ante phalaṃ sthitam // [AgMsv_2.280]

plain_english: The qualified person is truly one, the recipient of attaining Śiva-hood; even when the teaching appears only in limited sectional form, that single qualification and attainment remain.
sanskrit_cite:
adhikārī caika eva śivatāvāptibhājanam /
tathāpi tāvanmātre ca jāte prakaraṇātmani // [AgMsv_2.281]
